LEAFORA / BOTANICAL ARCHIVEFIELD NOTE 001

Herbarium report

Tomato

Early blight

SPECIMEN 01 · IMAGE STUDY
SPECIMENIllustrated sample leaf CONFIDENCEHigh STATUSIllustrative example

Early blight is a common fungal disease of tomato. Dark spots appear on older leaves first and spread upward in warm, humid weather.

Biological treatment

  • Remove and bin affected lower leaves; do not add them to compost.
  • Apply a biological control labelled for early blight, such as Bacillus subtilis, following the product label.

Chemical treatment

  • Use a fungicide registered for early blight on tomato and follow its label rate and interval.
  • Alternate active ingredients between sprays and respect the harvest period.

Care & prevention

  • Mulch around the base so soil does not splash onto lower leaves.
  • Rotate with non-tomato crops for at least two seasons.
  • Water early in the day, keep foliage dry and inspect new growth weekly.

AI-generated guidance. Check the local product label and ask an agricultural expert.
